{{short description|African American mathematician}}

'''Walter Richard Talbot''' (1909-1977)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Walter R. Talbot - Mathematicians of the African Diaspora|url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/talbot_walterr.html|access-date=2020-12-29|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> was the fourth [[African Americans|African American]] to earn a Ph.D. in [[Mathematics]] ([[Geometric group theory|Geometric Group Theory]]) from the [[University of Pittsburgh]]<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Hales|first=Thomas|date=2018-05-16|title=Walter Talbot's thesis|class=math.HO|eprint=1805.06890}}</ref> and [[Lincoln University (Pennsylvania)|Lincoln University]]'s youngest [[Doctor of Philosophy]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Walter R Talbot - Biography|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Talbot_Walter/|access-date=2020-12-29|website=Maths History|language=en}}</ref> He was a member of [[Sigma Xi]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Talitha|title=In Honor of Black History|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201802/rnoti-p118.pdf|website=www.ams.org}}</ref> and [[Phi Tau Phi|Pi Tau Phi]].<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B1gEAAAAMBAJ&q=Walter+Richard+Talbot%2C+Pi+Tau+Phi&pg=PA262|title=The Crisis|date=August 1931|publisher=The Crisis Publishing Company, Inc.|language=en}}</ref>
In 1969 Talbot co-founded the [[National Association of Mathematicians|National Association of Mathematics]] (NAM) at [[Morgan State University]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Nkwanta|first=Asamoah|title=African-American Mathematicians and the Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/centennial/African_Americans.pdf|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2020-12-29|archive-date=2020-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928030332/https://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/centennial/African_Americans.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> the organization which, nine years later honored him at a memorial luncheon and created a scholarship<ref>{{Cite web|last=Houston|first=Johnny|title=Ten African American Pioneers and Mathematicians Who Inspired Me|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201802/rnoti-p139.pdf|website=www.ams.org}}</ref> in his name.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pitcher|first=Everett|title=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/197108/197108FullIssue.pdf|website=www.ams.org}}</ref> In 1990 the Cox-Talbot lecture<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cox-Talbot Lecture|url=https://www.nam-math.org/cox-talbot-lecture.html|access-date=2020-12-29|website=www.nam-math.org|archive-date=2021-02-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214165933/https://www.nam-math.org/cox-talbot-lecture.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> was inaugurated recognizing his accomplishments together with [[Elbert Frank Cox]] – the first African-American to get a doctoral degree in mathematics.

Academic positions Talbot held include: Mathematics Department Chair and Professor<ref>{{Cite web|title=Document Resume|url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED084236.pdf}}</ref> (Morgan State University); assistant professor,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumni Vertical Files - Lincoln University|url=https://bluetigerportal.lincolnu.edu/web/browse-our-collections/alumni-vertical-files|access-date=2020-12-29|website=bluetigerportal.lincolnu.edu}}</ref> professor, department chair, dean of men, registrar, acting dean of instruction (Lincoln University).<ref>{{Cite book|last=Foundation (U.S.)|first=National Science|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qFgFAAAAMAAJ&q=walter+richard+talbot%2C+lincoln+university%2C&pg=PA261|title=Annual Report for Fiscal Year ...|date=1963|publisher=The Foundation|language=en}}</ref> Talbot was most widely known for his introduction of computer technology to the school.<ref>{{Cite news|date=December 29, 1977|title=Dr. Walter R. Talbot Sr.|work=The Baltimore Sun}}</ref>

Talbot's [[dissertation]] was entitled ''Fundamental Regions in S(sub 6) for the Simple Quaternary G(sub 60), Type I.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Walter R. Talbot: MathSciNet|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=42889|website=www.genealogy.math}}</ref>
